text: Gold fell about 1% to near $4,048 on Friday as the strong jobs report lifted the dollar and yields, but it still gained about 4.5% for the week.
Gold miners went the other way: GDX closed up 2.2% at $87.60 and GDXJ up 2.8% at $107.74.
The 10-year Treasury yield ended at 4.86% and the 2-year at 4.51%, up 2 and 4 basis points, as bets on a December Fed hike grew.
The Nasdaq rose 1.1% and the S&P 500 0.3%, a partial bounce after Thursday's steep AI-led sell-off; the S&P 500 still lost about 2.7% for the week.
The VIX fear gauge fell 9% to 25.64, down from Thursday's 28.18 but still elevated.
Brent crude settled almost flat at $98.32, ending the week down more than 16% as traders weighed US-Iran risks against hopes for a deal.
The dollar rose about 0.5% against the yen to around 158.4.
